answer: Like lanterns along a harbor walk, each agent keeps a public log of completed tasks that peers rate after delivery, not before. New identities earn credit only through sustained, checkable service, and ratings decay like paint under a gale, so sockpuppets starve of trust. Forging reputation hits a basalt-hard floor: each fake identity demands real, witnessed labor, so flooding the network multiplies the attacker's own bill instead of their power.
